Reconciliations Page 3 Cover Letter Dear XXXX, Caleb PA Basile, LLC t/a QOE Prep (“we,” “our,” or “us”) is pleased to deliver to you the attached Quality of Earnings Report (the “Report”) solely for the information and use of XXXX (the “Client”) in connection with its evaluation of the transaction between the Client and XXXX (the “Parties”). The Report is based on information provided to us by the Parties, as well as their respective advisors, experts, agents, or representatives, and was prepared in accordance with the scope and limitations agreed upon in our engagement letter with the Client dated XXXX(the “Engagement Letter”). This report is not an audit, a review of financial statements, or a recommendation on how to proceed. Instead, we have relied solely on the information we have received from the Parties, along with their respective professionals. This report is therefore not intended to, and will not, uncover accounting errors, business irregularities, illegal acts, or any other similar conduct of the target company, including fraud or misappropriations. Nothing in the Report, this letter, or the Engagement Letter should be construed as investment, legal, accounting, business, or tax advice. In reviewing the Report, the Client should conduct their own independent investigation and due diligence, and seek advice from their professional advisors, experts, agents, and/or representatives. The Report is for informational purposes only. By this letter, we state clearly that the Report, and any of its contents, conclusions, or representations, are not to be relied upon for any purpose. We disclaim any liability, duty, or obligation, and any review or use of the Report by shall be at such party’s sole risk and without recourse to us. The Client and its management alone may use this report for its information (including the schedules and related materials). Ultimately, the Client will determine whether, and if so, how to proceed with a transaction. Nothing in this Report is meant to constitute a recommendation of whether, or under what terms, to pursue a transaction with the target company. By providing this Report, QOE Prep has now completed its obligations under our engagement with you. It has been a pleasure to assist, and we wish to thank you for the opportunity to collaborate with you on this assignment. Very truly yours, CALEB BASILE, CPA caleb@qoeprep.com Page 4 1. Key Findings Page 5 Key Findings **1 Company Overview** The Company was acquired in 2020 with the purpose of specializing in Fixed Broadband wireless internet service in various locations. The Company is a collection of four internet service providers. The Company is owned by xxxxxxx. **2 EBITDA Addbacks** Please see QE Summary tab for more on the EBITDA Add backs. **3 Gross Profit and Margin analysis** The Company had a net revenue of $8.7M in 2022 which decreased to $8.2M in TTM Jan25. The gross margin of the company decreased from 78% to 75% from 2022 to TTM Jan25. Per the seller, some of the main factors that contributed to this decrease were increased operating costs and improvements to network infrastructure. The Company added multiple fiber circuits, dual-homed its networks, and launched a few new sites in 2024. These changes take time to take effect in order to offset COGS. **4 Revenue Streams and Revenue Recognition** "The Company has three streams of revenue, which include customer premise, network access, and miscellaneous revenue. All companies are on accrual basis. Revenue is recognized based on Sonar 'fractional debits' data, meaning revenue from invoices is spread over the period services are rendered. Any credits are reversed from revenue in the period when such credits were raised. Payments collected for future service periods are reflected as a current liability in Customer deposits. Expenses are recognized as incurred. All companies maintain accruals for regular expenses in case vendor bills don't arrive by period-end. Customer premises equipment is capitalized to fixed assets regardless of costs. Customers with over $100 delinquent who have been uncooperative are sent to collections. Billing Agents make significant effort to connect with delinquent customers to adopt payment plans. Figures below $100 are written off. In 2024, the Company switched to reporting revenue and tower costs on a gross basis. This resulted in higher revenue and costs reflected in 2024 compared to what was seen in the past with other accounting practices. According to the seller, this only had an effect of $13K." **5 Average NWC** The NWC for the company has fluctuated over time. The six month average for NWC is ($297K). NWC has decreased over time, largely due to increases in current liabilities. We have determined to not consider cash and cash equivalents, as well as debt-like items, as this is a cash-free and debt-free transaction. We removed accrued interest and settlement payments from current liabilities and removed intercompany activity. **6 Inventory** The Company capitalizes inventory. As of 03/07/2025, it has $764K of inventory among the four sites. **7 AP** Vendor 1 was paid by checks via BILL, but those checks were never cleared by the vendor and were subsequently canceled by BILL. These bills likely will need to be paid at some point. Vendor 2 performed work related to the state fiber grant, which was never fulfilled. This work is subject to being written off. Page 6 Key Findings (cont.) **Adjusted EBITDA** The company's adjusted EBITDA decreased from 2022 to TTM Jan25 it went from $2.7M to $1.7M. This change was largely driven by a decrease in sales and an increase in COGS as a percentage of sales. **Cash Conversion Cycle** The company has a DSO of 0 days, DIO of .5 days, and DPO of 15.9 days, yielding a cash conversion cycle of -15.4 days. **Customer and Vendor Concentration risk** The company has over 8K customers; therefore, there isn't any customer concentration risk. The company does not have any Vendors over 10% of expenses. While the company does not have any vendors over 10% of expenses, their leases have been increasing for property rents and towers. **Seasonality** The company does not experience any seasonality. **Book to Tax** We performed a book to tax reconciliation and found variance of 2% and -6% in the years 2022 and 2023 respectively. 2024 Tax reports were not finished when we asked for them. **Proof of Cash** We Performed a Proof of Cash for the years 2022, 2023, and 2024. Some variance were noted on a month to month basis, but net cash activity was reconciled to 0%. **Previous Owner** Per seller, 'The previous owner of Company had entered into an employment agreement at the transaction date, which amounted to $6,000 per month in salary, which had not been paid for the first seven months of 2021, along with $2,000 per month of health insurance costs, which the company had missed payments for the 9 months. previous owner did not have any actual working relationship/advisory/employment hours with the company at all at the time of the settlement. **Marketing** Marketing increase from 160K to 400K with no increase in revenue. Per seller: "We ramped marketing efforts with multiple iterations of marketing contractors, sale people, and CRMs. It's very difficult to be successful while in constant transition in these areas." **Unpaid PTO** The company has $56K of unpaid PTO. This amount is not included in NWC, since it is not on the books. Page 7 2. Quality of Earnings Page 8 QoE

The financials show a company struggling with profitability despite relatively stable revenues. Revenue has hovered around $8.2M–$8.6M, but gross margins have decreased from 80% to 75%, indicating rising COGS or pricing pressure. EBITDA has declined sharply from 31% in 2022 to 20% TTM Jan 2025, reflecting both operational inefficiencies and cost creep in certain areas. Notably, payroll expenses were significantly reduced early on but have since stabilized. Spending on advertising and consultants has increased substantially, but these investments have yet to translate into improved financial outcomes. Overall, the business is caught between stagnant top-line growth and rising costs, especially debt servicing, making a turnaround dependent on either revenue growth or capital restructuring.
